description: What null means in a plan: absent and null are the same, null meets the provider default, and null on an Optional+Computed argument keeps the state value. Facts come from the provider source catalogue (aws-replace.json).

cases.name: an argument added as null is no change, even when it forces replacement (source case: terraform-aws-rds-aurora 683c06916, log_group_class wired to a null variable)
a new Optional+Computed ForceNew argument set to null is no change (source case: terraform-aws-rds-aurora cf965379f, cluster_scalability_type)
an Optional argument without a default added as null is no change
null meeting the provider default is no change (source case: terraform-aws-rds-aurora 7ffa33f82, engine_mode null to "provisioned")
the provider default meeting an absent argument is no change
an Optional+Computed argument set to null keeps the state value: no change (source case: terraform-aws-rds-aurora e054f77c7, master_username "root" to null)
an Optional+Computed argument going from "" to null is no change (source case: terraform-aws-rds-aurora 52b2a14ec, database_name)
an Optional+Computed ForceNew argument going from null to a value is a possible replacement, reviewed not blocked (source case: terraform-aws-rds-aurora b792d84b6)
guard: a real change of an Optional+Computed ForceNew argument is still a proven replacement that blocks
guard: null meeting a value other than the provider default is still a proven replacement
guard: an Optional argument without a default going from null to a value is still a proven replacement
guard: "" and null are not equal when the argument has a provider default
in a plugin-framework resource an Optional+Computed ForceNew argument set to null may still be replaced: likely, not proven
an in-place argument added as null is no update
a forcing argument that only goes from absent to null is not named among the arguments that force a real replacement (source case: terraform-aws-rds-aurora 52b2a14ec)
